notes: Shared contract for tools/texgen/greenery.py (paints) and tools/blender/greenery.py (models). Rects are [x, y, w, h] from the image top-left (Blender v = 1 - y / h).

The game loads public/textures/map/<name>.png with THREE.TextureLoader and never sets wrapS/wrapT, so every texture CLAMPS: all UVs stay inside [0, 1]. 'tiles: u' below only means the strip is painted seamless left-right so neighbouring faces that each map the strip once line up; nothing relies on UV repeat.

Lighting in the game is one ambient light, no directional light, and vertex colours are ignored: form must come from the albedo. 'ramp' regions run light (top rows) to dark (bottom rows) and the modeler picks V per vertex from its smooth normal (up = light rows, sideways = middle, down = dark rows), so occlusion is baked through the UVs.
Cut-out textures are RGBA with hard alpha (0 or 255): the game alpha-tests at 0.5 with NearestFilter and no mips, so no feature is thinner than 2 px.

frond_lit.look: One palm frond lying along U: petiole base at x = 0, tip at x = 63. The rib runs along y = 16 (the card is folded along that row: rows 0-15 are one half, rows 16-31 the other). Leaflets leave the rib angled about 35 degrees toward the tip, each a 3 px wide tapered blade, 1-2 px dark gaps between them only in their outer half, so the inner half of each side is solid. Half-width grows from 3 px at the base to 14 px at x = 22 and tapers to 2 px at the tip. Colour warm palm green #3a5020 lifted to about (72, 98, 40) on top, leaflet tips yellower, the rib a 2 px pale olive line. Frond base (x < 10) browner and 35 % darker: occlusion at the crown. Alpha 255 inside the silhouette, 0 outside.

frond_shade.look: Same layout as frond_lit (rib on y = 48), different seed for the leaflet rhythm, a little narrower, drawn about 40 % darker and cooler: (40, 58, 26) average, with a few dry brown leaflet tips. Used on the lower, drooping and inner fronds so the crown reads as lit on top and shaded underneath.

trunk.look: The whole palm trunk once: U goes once around (seamless left-right), V runs from the crown (y = 0) to the foot (y = 51). Ring scars every 4 px: a 1 px dark groove, under it a 1 px lighter lip, the 2 px between in brown #6a4820 with fibre streaks; rings wobble +-1 px and the leaf-scar pattern offsets by half a step every other ring (diamond look). Rows 0-8 darken by up to 40 % (shadow under the crown); rows 44-51 darken 25 % with dirt.

crown.look: Crownshaft / boot: frond bases, dark olive-brown sheaths with fibre, (60, 52, 30) average, darkest (30 %) at the bottom row. Mapped on the knob where the fronds leave the trunk.

band.look: Gilded moulding strip, top of the image = top of the band: rows 0-1 bright gold lip (235, 200, 110), row 2 dark line, rows 3-5 a bead row (3 px bright beads every 4 px, dark between), rows 6-12 gilt body ramping from (200, 150, 55) to (150, 105, 35) with soft tarnish, row 13 dark groove, rows 14-15 darker foot (110, 75, 25). Opaque.

railing.look: Cut-out gilded railing, top of the image = top of the fence: top rail rows 16-18 (3 px), bottom rail rows 36-39 (4 px), balusters 2 px wide every 8 px (x = 3-4, 11-12, ...) with a 4 px collar knob at rows 26-28, and between each pair a 4 px gold lozenge hanging from the top rail (rows 19-23). Alpha 255 on metal, 0 in the gaps. Gold shaded lighter on the top edge of each rail, darker on the bottom edge.

gilt.look: Ramp of plain hammered gilt: row 40 brightest (245, 215, 120), row 63 darkest (85, 58, 20), smooth in V, mottled hammer dents (2-3 px) and a little brown tarnish in U. Opaque. Used on urns, pots, collars and ball finials, V picked from the vertex normal so they read rounded under flat light.

ramp.look: Clipped box hedge, small leaf clumps (2-3 px blobs with darker gaps, no single-pixel salt), seamless in U. A brightness ramp in V: row 0 lit top (88, 112, 44), row 16 the art bible's #3a4a18-ish body (58, 74, 30), row 31 deep interior shadow (22, 30, 12). Up-facing hedge uses the top rows, sides the middle, undersides (cap brim, moustache, chin, the bottom of a hedge) the bottom rows.

flowers_red.look: A bed of red flowers seen from above: 2x2 and 3x2 px heads in regime red (190, 30, 30) to (220, 60, 40), a lighter pixel on some, dark green leaves (40, 58, 22) in the gaps, about 55 % red. Mapped at about 5.5 px/unit in both axes on the bed polygons (never stretched to the rect), rows 46-47 darker (bed edge).

flowers_gold.look: Same as flowers_red in marigold gold (230, 170, 30) to (250, 210, 70), about 55 % flowers, rows 62-63 darker. Same mapping as flowers_red.

conc_side.look: Plain grey precast concrete planter wall (120, 118, 112) like stone.png, top = top of the wall: row 0 a lighter arris, a faint form-joint every 32 px, pores and small stains, bottom 4 rows darken to 60 % (ground contact and splash grime). Inner walls use rows 2-12 so they darken toward the soil.

conc_top.look: Rim top of the same concrete, 10 % lighter, a dark 1 px edge on rows 13 and 17.

poor_side.look: The same wall decayed: darker and dirtier (95, 92, 85), soot and rust-brown run streaks from the top, two or three dark 1-2 px cracks branching down from the rim, spalled patches showing lighter aggregate, green-black moss along the bottom 3 rows.

poor_top.look: Chipped rim: grey with dark chips eating into both edges, a crack crossing it.

marble_side.look: Polished pink-white marble curb (215, 195, 185) with grey-rose veins running diagonally, row 36 a bright arris, rows 41-42 darker (ground contact).

marble_top.look: Marble cap seen from above, lighter (225, 210, 200), veins, 1 px darker edges.

soil.look: Dark garden soil (60, 45, 32) with clods and a few pale grit pixels, darker toward the rect edges (planter wall occlusion).

soil_poor.look: Dry grey-brown dirt (78, 68, 54) with litter: cigarette butts (2x1 off-white), a bottle cap, paper scraps, dark wet patches; darker at the edges.

weeds.look: Dead weeds standing on the bottom edge: a dense dry tuft (rows 24-31 solid at the bottom), 6-8 stalks 2 px wide rising and splaying, grey-brown (110, 95, 70) to straw (150, 130, 90), a few seed heads (3x3 px), one stalk bent over. Alpha hard.

flowers.look: Garden flowers standing on the bottom edge: a leafy green clump at the bottom (rows 22-31 mostly solid), 2 px stems, 6 flower heads (3x3 to 4x4 px) in red, white and yellow at different heights, darker centres. Alpha hard.

glass.look: Green bottle glass, opaque: a dark green body (30, 70, 40) with a 2 px pale vertical highlight at x = 4-5, darker edges, a dirty band near the bottom. V runs bottom (row 47) to neck (row 32).

can.look: A crushed drink can, no brand: faded red band (150, 40, 35) across the middle, dented silver-grey top and bottom thirds, dark crease lines.

paper.look: Crumpled dirty newspaper: grey-beige (170, 165, 150) with darker fold lines and illegible grey column blocks (no letters), a brown stain.

rubble.look: Broken concrete fracture face: lighter raw aggregate (140, 135, 125) with dark pits, darker toward the edges. Used on the fallen chunk and the broken corner.

litter.look: Spare: a dry grass fringe standing on the bottom edge (rows 56-63 solid), 2 px blades, straw and grey-green. Used along the poor planter's broken rim.

env_tree_rich.envelope: Pivot = env_tree_medium's (its bbox centre): ground at z = -9.14, trunk foot centred at (0.15, -0.10). Palm about 26 tall (top near z = 17), canopy about 18 across. Gilded collar + railing cage at the foot.

env_planter_poor.envelope: Origin at the footprint centre, ground z = 0, 10 x 6, 2.2 tall walls.

env_planter_normal.envelope: Origin at the footprint centre, ground z = 0, 10 x 6, 2.2 tall walls, shrub to about 4.5.

env_planter_rich.envelope: Origin at the footprint centre, ground z = 0, 14 x 9: marble curb, gilded fence, hedge parterre, red and gold beds, gold urn to about 4.5.

env_bush_rich.envelope: Origin at the footprint centre, ground z = 0, about 4 x 4, 7.5 tall: gilded pot, hedge bust of the leader in a peaked cap, facing -Y.

palette_hint: Match public/textures/map/leaves.png (greens about (57, 79, 46)), trunk.png, stone.png (about 120 grey). Mid values, no directional light; occlusion baked. Gold is the dictator's colour; red flowers are the regime's red.
